newsitem.title: USA: EU meat negotiators back to Europe, no deal yet.
newsitem.headline: EU meat negotiators back to Europe, no deal yet.

text.p: EU officials trying to negotiate an agreement with the United States in a nasty dispute over meat imports left Washington Friday afternoon with no accord in hand, but officials said the two sides would remain in contact through the weekend.
"There is still no agreement ... The Europeans have departed for home," said Agriculture Department spokesman Jim Petterson.
Petterson said that although no further face-to-face falks have been scheduled yet, it would not be out of the question if further meetings were held next week.
"We are expecting to be in touch via fone and fax," said Petterson. "In other words, we are still talking."
Petterson said if no agreement has been reached by April 15, Washington still intends to proceed with its plan to remove over 100 European meat and poultry plants from its list of approved exporters.
"Right now that is still the plan -- to proceed with the delisting," he said.
That action could halt up to $300 million worth of EU meat shipments to the United States, mostly pork products from Denmark and Italian hams.
U.S. and EU officials have been meeting in Washington since Tuesday to try to work out a deal in the so-called verterinary equivalency talks.
Since April 1, U.S. poultry shipments potentially worth some $50 million have been halted to Europe due to new EU inspection rules.
Officials have been working to reach a deal by April 15 to avoid a further escalation of the dispute.
EU officials have threatened "quick and decisive" action if the United STates restricts imports of EU meat, but USDA warned Thursday that extending the April 15 deadline was not a possibility.
